counterexample: Tick spacing 10. Positions [50, 200) and [100, 200), so ticks 50, 100 and 200 are initialized. Start 100, end 40. Tick 50 is set in the same bitmap word below the start, so the current tick stays at 100 and the search begins at tick 90. The walk returns [50]; it should return [100, 50]. The liquidity left after the walk is the liquidity of [100, 200) instead of 0.

new_flaw.description: The patch removed the line that sets the current tick before the empty-range return. When start equals end, the current tick keeps its old value: 0 for a fresh iterator from initDown, or wherever the last walk stopped. At a negative tick this makes hasNext true, so the walk yields tick 0 and the initialized ticks between 0 and the current tick, none of which the swap crossed. Example: tick spacing 60, pool at tick -300 with active liquidity L1, and a position [0, 600) with liquidity L2 larger than L1. A taxed zero-for-one swap that stays inside tick -300 gets tick 0 from the walk, the hook subtracts its net liquidity L2 from L1, and afterSwap reverts with ArithmeticOverflowUnderflow. Anyone can add such a position to block these swaps.

summary: Sets the current tick to the start plus one only when no initialized tick lies below the start in the same bitmap word; otherwise the start tick is still skipped. It also stops setting the current tick for an empty range, so hasNext can be true when start equals end.
